title: Windows 11 prerequisites for afox
description:
Inventory of what afox needs on Windows 11 with no WSL, and what is missing. Measured on this machine 2026-09-18.

Present: node 26.7.0, npm 11.19.0, git 2.55.0, Git Bash (MSYS2 bash 5.3), perl, timeout, awk, sed, Windows PowerShell 5.1. Provider CLIs present: claude, codex, ollama.
Absent: tmux, zsh, uuidgen, WSL, pwsh 7, go, docker. Provider CLIs absent: devin, gemini, goose, opencode.

Open items beyond the raw list:
- ~/.tmux.conf is created by fleet.sh as a symlink; on Windows that needs Developer Mode or an elevated shell, otherwise ln silently produces a copy or fails.
- The cost manifest path is ${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/afox-fleet-*.json. TMPDIR is normally unset on Windows, so it falls back to /tmp, which under MSYS2 is a private mount, not C:\Temp - fine, but it means a Windows-native node process and an MSYS node process disagree about where the manifest is.
- cost.mjs resolves provider session logs from node's homedir(); MSYS node and Windows node return different roots, so the log discovery has to be pinned to one of them.
acceptance_criteria: A written prerequisite list in the repo that someone can follow on a clean Windows 11 box to the point where FLEET_DRY_RUN=1 ./fleet.sh composes every pane command without error. Each missing item either installed, replaced, or recorded as not needed.

title: Beads on Windows: install, configure, state tracked in the repo
description:
bd was installed only on the Mac. On this Windows 11 machine there was no bd binary, and the Dolt database is gitignored and was never pushed, so the tracker was empty here: the ticket bodies existed on one machine only.

Install @beads/bd from npm (it ships win32 x64), initialise against the existing .beads/ without disturbing metadata.json's project_id, and make ticket state travel with the repo as .beads/issues.jsonl so any machine can read it after a git pull.

Deliberately NOT done: no Dolt push to the git remote, and no attempt to replace or reach the Mac's Dolt database. Cross-machine carry is JSONL interchange (upsert on import), which is additive and cannot clobber a database it never touches.
acceptance_criteria: bd --version works on Windows with no WSL; bd list runs against the repo's .beads/; .beads/issues.jsonl is tracked in git and contains the open tickets; .beads/metadata.json project_id unchanged from the Mac's value; no-push is true so bd never pushes to origin unprompted.
notes: Observed 2026-09-18: npm i -g @beads/bd installed 1.3.0; bd init -p afox --skip-agents --skip-hooks --non-interactive reported 'Remote has no Dolt data yet; initialized a fresh local database'; metadata.json content identical to the pre-init copy apart from line endings; config.yaml untouched by init. --skip-agents was passed on purpose so bd could not rewrite the hand-written AGENTS.md.
close_reason: Observed on this Windows 11 machine 2026-09-18, no WSL. npm i -g @beads/bd installed 1.3.0; 'bd --version' prints 1.3.0 (f45b249ce) and 'bd where' resolves C:\_____\_CODE\afox\.beads. 'bd list' before init printed 'no beads database found' and wrote nothing, confirming the tracker was empty here and that nothing was overwritten. 'bd init -p afox --skip-agents --skip-hooks --non-interactive --role maintainer' reported 'Remote has no Dolt data yet; initialized a fresh local database'; --skip-agents kept it away from the hand-written AGENTS.md. .beads/metadata.json is byte-identical to the pre-init copy apart from line endings, so project_id f3529f2e-df73-4eae-a734-119313717e43 is unchanged; config.yaml was untouched by init. export.auto and export.git-add set true, no-push set true. 'bd export' wrote 8 issues to .beads/issues.jsonl and 'git check-ignore' confirms it is trackable. The Mac's Dolt database was never contacted: the only cross-machine channel configured is JSONL, which imports as an upsert.

title: Reconcile the Mac's Beads database into the repo
description:
The pre-existing tickets - afox-99q (the merge/review gate cycle), afox-2fc (pane lifecycle) and afox-5lf (v1 multiplexer) - live only in the Mac's Dolt database. It is gitignored, was never pushed, and the remote has no Dolt data, so their descriptions and acceptance criteria cannot be read from this machine.

They were deliberately NOT recreated here. Recreating them under their own ids would upsert over the Mac's originals on the next import and destroy acceptance criteria nobody can currently read; recreating them under new ids would leave permanent duplicates.

When the Mac is available: git pull there first so the Windows tickets arrive, bd import .beads/issues.jsonl (upsert, additive - it does not replace the database), then bd export so the JSONL carries the full set, and commit. After that both machines see everything and afox-2fc and afox-99q can be worked from either.

afox-5lf has no description and no acceptance criteria and reads as the original v1 umbrella epic. Decide then: close it as superseded, or rewrite it as the tracking epic for the Windows port.
acceptance_criteria: bd list on Windows shows afox-99q, afox-2fc and afox-5lf with the descriptions they were created with on the Mac; .beads/issues.jsonl in git contains every ticket from both machines; the Mac's Dolt database was added to, never replaced.

title: Run afox on Windows without WSL
description:
afox is zsh + tmux. Windows has neither, WSL is not installed and is not wanted. Three routes were considered; the ticket starts as a spike, not a build.

(a) MSYS2. pacman -S tmux zsh, fleet.sh runs close to unchanged. Cheapest by an order of magnitude. The whole route hangs on one unknown: whether a full-screen agent TUI (claude) renders correctly inside an MSYS2 tmux pane, or whether the ConPTY-to-MSYS-pty boundary mangles it. Spike this first on one pane before planning anything else.

(b) PowerShell + Windows Terminal. Rejected. wt.exe splits panes but offers no pane addressing, no capture-pane, no pane-border-format and no per-pane user options. Every mechanism afox depends on - roles on borders, send-keys, capture, cost display - has no equivalent.

(c) Own the PTY. A node host using node-pty/ConPTY spawns each provider and afox renders the panes itself. Gives real addressing, capture better than capture-pane, our own borders, and drops tmux and zsh entirely. The cost is honest and large: compositing several full-screen TUI agents means embedding a terminal emulator (xterm headless plus a renderer). That is writing a tmux. Only reach for it if (a) fails.

Decide (a) or (c) on the spike result, not on preference.
acceptance_criteria: Spike first: MSYS2 tmux installed, one pane running claude, and a capture-pane of that pane recorded showing whether the TUI is intact or corrupted. Then either a fleet spawned on Windows with every pane showing its role on the border, or a written finding that route (a) is dead and why, with the evidence.

title: Replace uuidgen with node crypto.randomUUID in fleet.sh
description:
fleet.sh calls uuidgen to mint the --session-id it hands to claude and records in the cost manifest. uuidgen does not exist in Git Bash, MSYS2 or any stock Windows shell, so the call fails on Windows and takes the whole fleet window with it (a dying pane command makes tmux drop the window silently - the standing gotcha in README).

node is already a hard requirement of fleet.sh, so use it: node -e 'console.log(crypto.randomUUID())'. Same lowercase hyphenated form, one less binary to install.
acceptance_criteria: fleet.sh mints session ids without uuidgen on PATH; FLEET_DRY_RUN=1 ./fleet.sh prints a well-formed lowercase UUID in each claude pane's --session-id.
notes: Change made 2026-09-18: fleet.sh now mints the session id with node -e 'process.stdout.write(crypto.randomUUID())'. Partially observed only - the node call itself was run on this Windows machine and printed 35511a4f-1d6a-46d5-a0b1-689f6dc0407c, but the acceptance criterion needs FLEET_DRY_RUN=1 ./fleet.sh, and fleet.sh is zsh, which is not installed here. Left in_progress rather than closed on an argument; it closes when a shell exists to run it in (afox-r0s).

title: Repository structure: modules and domain boundaries
description:
Root is flat: six markdown files, five .sh/.mjs scripts, three .yml, no boundaries. Proposal, deliberately sequenced after the typing decision so nothing gets moved twice:

  bin/                 entry point
  src/config|fleet|cost|board|gate/
  config/              roles.yml providers.yml prices.yml (user-editable, stays obvious)
  docs/                SPECS.md COMPARISON.md ACTIVE-LISTENING.md
  README.md AGENTS.md  stay at root

Three traps to respect:
- tmux.conf is the symlink target of ~/.tmux.conf. Moving it dangles every existing link. fleet.sh re-points the link on each run so it is survivable, but it needs a comment recording why.
- AGENTS.md and README.md must not move: every provider looks for them at the root.
- ${0:A:h}, roles.yml's repo: . and the manifest path are all path-derived. Each move is a real edit, not a git mv.
acceptance_criteria: Every script runs from its new location; FLEET_DRY_RUN=1 ./fleet.sh composes identical pane commands before and after the move, diffed; a fresh clone plus setup.sh still produces a working fleet command.

title: Types for afox config: zod schemas over JSON, no decorators
description:
Original question was whether to convert afox into a TypeScript-with-decorators project resembling Java 21. Answer: no to the Java facsimile, yes to types.

Decorators would mean @Role({provider, tools}) classes, which moves per-role config out of roles.yml and back into code. That is a regression against SPECS #5 (per-role config), one of afox's strongest columns in COMPARISON.md, and against the role skill's own rule that roles are data. DI and annotations solve a problem five roles and no injection graph do not have.

What is worth doing: roles.mjs and cost.mjs each carry a separate hand-rolled mini-YAML parser, and fleet.sh uses a 0x1f-delimited field protocol (README gotcha 6) purely because that data crosses a shell boundary. One typed loader with zod schemas over JSON deletes both parsers and the delimiter trick, and gives a real error when a config field is wrong instead of silent garbage.

Open question the ticket must settle: JSON as the on-disk format costs roles.yml its comments and its prompt: | block scalars, which are the most readable part of the file today. Either keep YAML on disk and validate with zod after parsing, or move to JSON and accept losing the comments.
acceptance_criteria: A single typed config loader replaces the parsers in roles.mjs and cost.mjs; a malformed roles entry produces a named field error instead of a shifted field or an empty string; FLEET_DRY_RUN=1 composes identical pane commands before and after the change, diffed.

title: tmux pane borders are indistinguishable from pane content
description:
The lines separating panes render in the same colour and weight as the text inside them, so a five-pane fleet reads as one wall of text and it is hard to tell which agent said what.

Likely cause: borders draw in the default foreground on the same background as pane text, and pane-border-lines is at its default single. Candidate fix, all in tmux.conf: pane-border-lines heavy or double, pane-border-style fg dimmed, pane-active-border-style a bright fg plus bold, and reverse video on the role segment of pane-border-format so it reads as a title bar rather than a line of text.

Cheap and self-contained, but AGENTS.md is explicit that a styling claim is only real once seen on a live window - which on Windows means this waits for a working tmux.
acceptance_criteria: A live fleet window screenshot or capture showing pane borders clearly distinct from pane content, and the active pane distinct from the inactive ones. Every setting recorded in tmux.conf, never in ~/.tmux.conf.
